title: Mind common definitions
description: PROPOSED (KOS-MIND-001, contract 0.1.0-draft). Shared definitions for the Mind request, context and result schemas. Timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time in UTC; durations carry their unit in the field name (_ms).

Digest.description: Algorithm-prefixed digest, for example sha256:<64 hex characters>.

Reference.description: A reference to an immutable snapshot or to a source record held elsewhere.

source_contract.description: Name and version of the contract the referenced record follows (for a Sense observation, the versioned Sense contract).

Uncertainty.description: A score alone is not uncertainty: the scale, source and calibration state are stated, and qualitative notes and assumptions are allowed.

scale.description: Meaning and range of the score, for example 'probability 0..1'.

code.description: Mind error codes. A Sense error code seen on an input is passed in detail.sense_error_code, never as this code.

Precondition.description: An informational claim about what Mind assumed. Consumers do not evaluate `expression`. A precondition that a consumer must resolve or enforce names a consumer-defined one through precondition_id.

precondition_id.description: Optional name of a precondition defined by the consumer (for Skill, in its manifest).

expression.description: Descriptive only; never evaluated by Mind or Skill.

ProposedSkill.description: A recommendation to Skill. It is not an authorization: Skill resolves the reference, validates its manifest, version and preconditions, and decides. proposal_id is unique within a result (a rule a validator must check; JSON Schema cannot). priority orders candidates and nothing more: a lower value is preferred (0 first); equal priorities, and absent priorities, are ordered by ascending proposal_id; a proposal with no priority comes after every proposal that has one.

ExecutionRecord.description: Reasoning execution record: enough to reconstruct recorded conditions, verify input and output digests and classify replay fidelity. Only the replay class and the input are always required, so a request that failed or was cancelled before any inference ran can still be recorded without invented model or output data. A COMPLETED or PARTIAL result must carry the full record (see mind-result). input, output and context_snapshot, when present, carry a digest so integrity can be verified. A COMPLETED or PARTIAL result must also carry a context_snapshot (see mind-result).

placement.description: Where the reasoning provider ran, when known: EDGE, NEXUS or CLOUD. Optional; a provider change is traceable through provider_id and, when recorded, placement.

ObservationRef.description: A reference to one Sense sample, by identity and clock, never by embedding Sense internals. The measurements of a STALE, MISSING or INVALID sample are not usable as readings (Sense contract section 6), so usable must be false for them. Clocks are not comparable across monotonic and utc.

usable.description: Mind's own freshness and validity decision for this observation.

source_contract.description: Sense contract version the sample follows, for example 0.1.0.

FreshnessPolicy.description: How Mind, as a consumer, judges freshness of Sense samples (Sense contract section 6.1): the maximum age in nanoseconds, with an optional per-sensor override. Freshness needs the consumer's now on the same clock as the sample; without it, freshness is not evaluated.

SkillId.description: Lowercase dotted skill name, the same shape as a Sense sensor_id. Stable across versions; never reused for a different skill.

VersionConstraint.description: Closed grammar: exact 1.2.3; caret ^1.2.0; range >=1.2.0 <2.0.0. No wildcards, tags or pre-release versions. Semantics (normative for this contract, not left to a SemVer library default): exact matches only that version; caret ^X.Y.Z matches versions >= X.Y.Z with the same MAJOR when MAJOR is not 0, or with the same MINOR when MAJOR is 0; a range matches versions >= the lower bound and < the upper bound, and a range whose lower bound is not strictly below its upper bound is invalid (a validator rule; the pattern cannot express it). A constraint selects among versions the consumer already holds; it is never a pin and never an approval.
